shadows.name: floating

narrative.overview:
Aliyah Estate reads like a glossy real-estate magazine spread, not a listings portal. Every surface is square-edged and photo-forward: full-bleed property imagery, generous whitespace, and serif display type doing the persuading while the interface itself recedes. The palette is dominated by near-black "ink" — primary buttons, badges, the footer band — with a muted bronze/gold accent (#856738/#C5A880) that appears only in small, deliberate doses: an icon, a link, a hover state, an eyebrow label. Gold is a wax seal, not a wash.

The system deliberately rejects the generic real-estate-portal look: no rounded pill cards, no blue hyperlinks, no dense MLS-style data grids, no stock-carousel sameness. Corners stay sharp everywhere except the handful of circular icon affordances (avatars, carousel dots, close buttons) that exist purely as touch targets. Depth comes from hairline borders and alternating background bands, not drop shadows — shadow is reserved for things that genuinely float above the page (a sticky search bar, a mobile filter drawer), so its rare appearance still reads as an interruption worth noticing.
keyCharacteristics: Serif display headlines (Cormorant Garamond) paired with an italicized, light-weight word for editorial emphasis
Near-black "ink" as the dominant primary color; bronze/gold accent used on a strict minority of any screen
Square edges everywhere except icon-only circles
Flat by default; shadow appears only on overlays that float above page flow
Uppercase, letter-spaced labels (0.1em) as section eyebrows and micro-navigation

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The bronze/gold accent (#856738/#C5A880) never fills a large surface. It marks icons, links, labels, badges, and hover states — always a minority of any given screen. Ink carries the visual weight instead.

rules.name: No New Hex Rule
rules.body: Every color used in the UI resolves to a token in this palette. A new arbitrary hex value is never introduced ad hoc — add a token here first.

rules.name: The Editorial Italic Rule
rules.body: Within a serif display headline, exactly one word or phrase is set in italic, lighter weight for emphasis — never the whole headline, never more than one phrase.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow only appears on something that is genuinely floating above the page — never on a card or button sitting in normal flow. A hover lift (transform only, no shadow) is not an exception to this.

rules.name: The Accent Draws In
rules.body: The one recurring motion motif: a thin accent-colored rule scales in from the left, once, wherever an eyebrow label or the active nav link needs an underline. Reused everywhere instead of inventing a new effect per surface.

rules.name: The Sharp Edge Rule
rules.body: Border-radius is 0 on every content surface (button, card, input, badge, panel). rounded-full is used only for icon-sized circular controls — never for cards, buttons with text, or images.

dos: Do keep every content surface square-edged (0px radius) — buttons, cards, inputs, badges, panels.
Do reserve rounded-full strictly for icon-only circles (arrow marks, dots, close buttons, count pills).
Do treat the bronze/gold accent as a rare mark — icons, links, labels, one emphasized CTA — never a large fill (The One Voice Rule).
Do alternate section backgrounds between Parchment Ground and Sable Sand, divided by hairline borders, to build rhythm without shadow.
Do set exactly one word or phrase in italic serif within a display headline for emphasis (The Editorial Italic Rule).
Do use uppercase, 0.1em-tracked labels as section eyebrows and micro-navigation text.
Do resolve every UI color to an existing token; add a new token before reaching for a new hex value.
donts: Don't add box-shadow to a card or button sitting in normal page flow — shadow is reserved for elements that float above the page (drawers, dropdowns, the sticky search bar).
Don't fill a large surface with the accent gold; it reads as decoration, not signal, at that scale.
Don't round the corners of a card, button, or input — that's the generic real-estate-portal look this system explicitly rejects.
Don't reach for blue links, dense MLS-style data grids, or stock-carousel sameness — the incumbent anti-reference this system was built against.
